nodes.name: MOFs Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co²⁺, Cu²⁺, Ni²⁺, and Zn²⁺ cations were first coordinated with the ligand of 2-methylimidazole, forming uniform MOFs support in the shape of rhombic dodecahedron.
nodes.source_text: Co²⁺, Cu²⁺, Ni²⁺, and Zn²⁺ cations were first coordinated with the ligand of 2-methylimidazole, forming uniform MOFs support...

unit_operations.name: Coordination
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Co²⁺, Cu²⁺, Ni²⁺, and Zn²⁺ cations were first coordinated with the ligand of 2-methylimidazole

nodes.name: MOFs Calcination
nodes.procedure: Thermal calcination treatment in argon was then conducted to carbonize the MOFs support (please see Supporting Information for details), after which only the XRD peaks of graphitic carbon were identified. The calcined MOFs support retained the rhombic dodecahedron morphology and the node metal components (Co, Cu, Ni, and Zn) were homogeneously dispersed throughout the MOFs skeleton.
nodes.source_text: Thermal calcination treatment in argon was then conducted to carbonize the MOFs support (please see Supporting Information for details)...

unit_operations.name: Calcination
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Thermal calcination treatment in argon was then conducted to carbonize the MOFs support

nodes.name: Pt Precursor Impregnation
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, Pt precursors (K₂PtCl₄) were impregnated onto the calcined MOFs support. By virtue of the N-metal coordination, Pt element was uniformly distributed on the calcined MOFs support.
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, Pt precursors (K₂PtCl₄) were impregnated onto the calcined MOFs support. By virtue of the N-metal coordination...

unit_operations.name: Impregnation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Pt precursors (K₂PtCl₄) were impregnated onto the calcined MOFs support. By virtue of the N-metal coordination

nodes.name: Hydrogen Reduction Alloying
nodes.procedure: As further revealed by the temperature-programmed H₂ reduction (H₂ TPR) spectrum, the reduction peak corresponding to the node metals of the calcined MOFs showed an 80°C decrease in the presence of Pt. To sufficiently alloy Pt and node metals, hydrogen reduction treatment at 600°C (much higher than that of the reduction temperature of node metals) was performed for the calcined MOFs support with Pt precursors' impregnation. After which ultrafine quinary PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloys were formed on the MOFs support.

unit_operations.name: H₂ Reduction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: hydrogen reduction treatment at 600°C... ultrafine quinary PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloys were formed

nodes.description: LSV evaluation of alkaline HER performance in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: These ultrafine nanoalloys with versatile metal components were then employed for electrochemical alkaline HER evaluations in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte. It was demonstrated by the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves in Figure 4a,b that those ultrafine nanoalloys exhibited substantially higher HER activity than the commercial Pt/C catalyst with a similar Pt weight loading (5 wt%) to them both in view of geometric activity (Figure 4a) and mass activity (Figure 4b)... the ultrafine quinary PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy exhibited a 15 mV decrease of reaction potential relative to that of the benchmark commercial 20 wt% Pt/C catalyst to deliver a 10 mA cm^{-2} current density (33 vs 45 mV)... When the current density output was set at 100 mA cm^{-2}, the reaction potential of the ultrafine quinary PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy became 40 mV lower than that of the commercial 20 wt% Pt/C catalyst (121 vs 161 mV)... the Tafel slope of the ultrafine PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy (46 mV dec^{-1})... the reaction potential to deliver 10 mA cm^{-2} current density over the ultrafine PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy catalyst remained stable at ≈ -33 mV for up to 120 h test. In the meanwhile, the LSV curve of the ultrafine PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy kept unchanged even after 7000 CV cycles' measurement.

nodes.characterization_summary: After thermal calcination in argon, only XRD peaks of graphitic carbon were identified.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermal calcination treatment in argon was then conducted to carbonize the MOFs support... after which only the XRD peaks of graphitic carbon were identified (Figure S13, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPR spectrum of calcined MOFs with Pt precursors showed reduction peak of node metals decreased by 80°C, indicating strong metal-metal interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As further revealed by the temperature-programmed H2 reduction (H2 TPR) spectrum in Figure S17 (Supporting Information), the reduction peak corresponding to the node metals of the calcined MOFs showed an 80°C decrease in the presence of Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images showed the morphology of the reduced MOFs support remained as the rhombic dodecahedron.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low-magnification scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images in Figures 2a and S18 (Supporting Information) and the TEM image in Figure 2b showed that the morphology of the reduced MOFs support remained as the rhombic dodecahedron.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM showed ultrafine nanoparticles on the MOFs support with average particle size of 1.3 ± 0.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images in Figure 2c,d clearly indicated the presence of ultrafine nanoparticles on the MOFs support with an average particle size of 1.3 ± 0.3 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM revealed well-defined lattice fringes of ultrafine nanoparticle with interplanar spacing of 0.208 nm along (111) direction and fcc crystallographic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM image of an ultrafine nanoparticle in Figure 2e revealed its well-defined lattice fringes and corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) patterns of the particle in the inset of Figure 2e disclosed its face-centered cubic (fcc) crystallographic structure.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elementary mapping analysis confirmed both Pt element and node metal elements (Co, Cu, Ni, and Zn) coexisted in the ultrafine nanoparticle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As was further verified by the EDS elementary mapping analysis in Figure 2g,h, both the Pt element and the node metal elements (Co, Cu, Ni, and Zn) coexisted in the ultrafine nanoparticle.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES spectra at Zn K-edge, Ni K-edge, Co K-edge, Cu K-edge, and Pt L-edge showed copresence of all metal components with electron transfer between metals; EXAFS confirmed Pt-Pt and Pt-M (M=Co,Cu,Ni,Zn) coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As demonstrated in Figure 3a-e, the well-resolved near-edge XAFS spectra (XANES) showed copresence of the Pt, Co, Cu, Ni, and Zn components in the catalyst.

properties.description: Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure experimental data

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS showed Pt, Co, and Cu components more electron-rich with lower binding energies; Ni showed increased Ni 2p3/2 binding energy indicating electron loss.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the electron transfer between these metal components in the ultrafine PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy was also verified by the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurement.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt loadings of ultrafine nanoalloys were ≈5 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To be noted, the Pt loadings of these ultrafine nanoalloys were ≈5 wt% determined by an inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) as summarized in Table S3 (Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman showed Raman peaks at ≈1200 cm⁻¹ (δ_Co-OH-Co) and 1550 cm⁻¹ (δ_Pt-OH-Pt) that intensified with decreasing potential, evidencing gradient OH transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Figure 5a, two Raman vibration peaks at ≈1200 and 1550 cm⁻¹ were clearly identified over the ultrafine PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy... which suggested that the two Raman vibration peaks were correlated with the intermediates produced during the alkaline HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV showed OH desorption peak of PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy positively shifted to 0.6 V vs other nanoalloys, indicating more facile OH desorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As demonstrated in Figure 4g, the OH desorption peak of the ultrafine PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy displayed an obvious positive shift compared with that of the ultrafine PtCoCuZn nanoalloy... Notably, the OH desorption potential of the ultrafine PtCoCuNiZn nanoalloy (0.6 V) exhibited a 40 mV increase relative to that of the ultrafine PtCoCuZn nanoalloy (0.56 V).
